title: Emit audit events for data residency + retention setting changes (tenant/project scope)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Context
- We need audit coverage for “sensitive actions” related to data residency/region and data retention settings across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Enterprise prospects (esp. Private) expect consistent semantics and before/after values for investigations + SOC2/ISO evidence.
- This ticket covers control-plane (and any shared config services) emission of audit events when residency/retention settings are changed at tenant or project scope.

Scope
In-scope config surfaces (initial)
- Tenant-level:
  - Default data residency region (e.g., where audit logs/metadata are stored; also influences control plane data residency for tenant config where applicable)
  - Default retention policy (audit log retention days; and any “request/trace retention” settings if configured via the same surface)
- Project-level overrides:
  - Project residency override (if supported)
  - Project retention override (if supported)

Out-of-scope for this ticket
- Implementing the residency/retention feature itself (we’re auditing changes, not building the configuration product).
- Customer-facing UI improvements beyond what’s needed to ensure the backend emits correct events.
- Data plane runtime routing changes (policy engine) — covered by ENG-4838.

Event taxonomy (proposed)
Coordinate with sensitive-actions taxonomy registry (ENG-4822) so the exact event_type names are registered and required fields are enforced.

Proposed event types (names may change based on final registry):
1) tenant.data_residency.updated
2) project.data_residency.updated
3) tenant.data_retention.updated
4) project.data_retention.updated

Each event must:
- Include “before” and “after” values in a bounded, low-cardinality way (no free-form JSON blobs; no arbitrary key dumping).
- Capture the scope (tenant vs project), and both IDs where applicable.
- Include correlation identifiers (request_id, trace_id, admin_action_id where present) per ENG-4830.
- Include actor attribution (who initiated the change; include impersonation / automation identity where supported by auth context).

Field expectations (aligned with schema v1 / flattened fields w/ namespaced extensions)
Required (from schema v1)
- schema_version
- event_id (ULID/UUID per platform standard; must be stable across retries)
- event_type (one of the above)
- occurred_at
- env (prod/stage), deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private)
- tenant_id
- actor_type + actor_id (user/service)
- actor_ip (when available; for Private operator flows may be “unknown” per policy, but must be explicit)
- source (service name, build/version)
- request_id / trace_id (best-effort if asynchronous)

Additional required fields for this taxonomy (to be enforced by registry/lints)
- scope_type: tenant | project
- scope_id: <tenant_id or project_id>
- target_type: tenant | project (same as scope_type unless we support “tenant updates project policy” semantics)
- target_id
- change_field: residency_region | retention_days | retention_mode (if applicable)
- previous_value: string (enum or normalized numeric-as-string)
- new_value: string

Notes on allowed values / cardinality
- residency_region must be an allow-listed region string (e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1). No arbitrary customer-provided region names.
- retention_days should be stringified integer (e.g., “30”, “90”), and MUST NOT include customer notes.
- If we support “retention_mode” (e.g., default vs locked), it must be an enum.

Redaction / sensitive data handling
- Do not log any secrets/tokens.
- Do not include full policy documents or config blobs in the event.
- If the setting change includes a “justification” text field in the API (some customers request this), do not include it in audit logs until reviewed by Security/GRC. If present, log “justification_present=true/false” only.
- Align with redaction rules and review checklist in ENG-4832.

Implementation plan
1) Identify codepaths
- Control plane endpoints that mutate residency/retention:
  - PATCH /v1/tenants/:tenant_id/settings (or equivalent)
  - PATCH /v1/projects/:project_id/settings (or equivalent)
- Any internal admin endpoints / console backend service-to-service endpoints that apply these changes.

2) Emit audit events
- On successful commit of the config transaction, emit the corresponding audit event.
- Include previous_value and new_value from the persisted config, not from request payload (avoid logging invalid/partial input).
- For multi-field updates (e.g., user changes both residency and retention in one request): emit one event per change_field to keep events consistent, searchable, and to avoid unbounded nested diffs.

3) Backcompat / normalization
- If legacy events exist for these settings (e.g., “tenant_settings_updated”), coordinate with ENG-4833/ENG-4827 to normalize or dual-emit during the migration window.
- Ensure schema_version is tagged and exporter validation passes.

4) Tests
- Unit tests: ensure event payload includes required taxonomy fields and uses allow-listed values.
- Integration tests: update tenant/project settings and assert an audit event is produced and validates against schema v1 (can be added to the suite in ENG-4834, but we should add local service-level integration tests here).
- Negative tests: ensure no event is emitted on failed validation / rejected update.

5) Private parity
- Ensure the same event_type + field semantics are emitted in Private when the settings are changed via Private control plane.
- For Private deployments where actor_ip/operator identity is unavailable, follow the standard: actor_ip="unknown" and actor_id derived from auth context if present; otherwise actor_id="system" with actor_type="service" (confirm with Security Eng before shipping).

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Event types are registered in the central taxonomy registry and pass build-time linting.
- [ ] Tenant-level residency change emits tenant.data_residency.updated with required fields + before/after values.
- [ ] Project-level residency override emits project.data_residency.updated with required fields + before/after values.
- [ ] Tenant-level retention policy change emits tenant.data_retention.updated with required fields + before/after values.
- [ ] Project-level retention override emits project.data_retention.updated with required fields + before/after values.
- [ ] Events validate against audit-log-schema-v1 (no exporter-side drops).
- [ ] No PII/secrets or free-form policy blobs are logged.
- [ ] Correlation IDs are present for synchronous flows; best-effort propagation for async flows is documented.
- [ ] Verified in at least one Private fixture environment and one Hosted staging environment.

Open questions
- Do we need separate event types for “locked retention” vs “retention days updated”? (Leaning: keep change_field to distinguish; avoid event type explosion.)
- Should “scope_id” always be the project_id for project events, while tenant_id remains a top-level required field? (Preferred: yes; makes SIEM searches consistent.)
- Are there any residency/retention settings applied at org/workspace scope distinct from “tenant”? If yes, add scope_type="org" with separate event types (confirm with Naomi/Olga).

Execution notes / progress
- 2026-02-06 (Michael Nguyen): Found two mutation paths: Console -> console-backend -> control-plane settings API, and internal admin CLI -> control-plane. Both converge on SettingsService.Update* but current audit emission is only on the Console backend layer (and it’s missing before/after). Plan is to move emission to control-plane service to avoid coverage gaps.
- 2026-02-14 (Ethan Park): Confirmed we should emit one event per change_field for multi-field updates to keep events SIEM-friendly.
- 2026-02-19 (Hanae Suzuki): Requested we do NOT include “reason/justification” text field in the audit event without explicit review; track as follow-up if needed.

Follow-ups (not required for close)
- Add coverage dashboard expected/observed mapping for these new event types (ENG-4828).
- If customers request “change request ticket id” capture, add a bounded field with allowlist/format validation (future enhancement).
comments: 2026-02-10 (Naomi Feldman): Please ensure we can demonstrate before/after values to auditors; screenshots from the coverage dashboard will be used as SOC2 evidence so consistent naming matters.

2026-02-12 (Olga Petrov): For evidence, we need to show that changes are attributable (actor) and scoped (tenant vs project). Also confirm retention statement is aligned with policy docs—don’t log anything that implies retention beyond contractual settings.

2026-02-20 (Logan Wright): Once event_type names are final, drop them in the expected-events config for the coverage dashboard; we’ll alert if we see “tenant settings updated” legacy events without normalized v1 events.

2026-02-22 (Kevin Osei): Exporter will dedupe on event_id; please make sure event_id is generated once per mutation, not per retry. If UpdateSettings is retried due to transient DB errors, do not emit duplicates on failed attempts.
